Finding.Text: The new default at skills/grace5-orchestrate/SKILL.md:17 continues in the same worktree after parking an unclosed change, but the standing method at models/architecture/method.md:56 and the unchanged executor at skills/grace5-execute/SKILL.md:15 still require "One change per worktree". Cited rationale entry L-07 at line 13 specifically relies on that isolation: "The boundary is the worktree, so the diff is the change", at a cost of a worktree per change. L-24 was added without reconciling L-07 or the lifecycle rule. This is observable in the required rehearsal: final status lists C2's two.txt and C3's three.txt outside C1's complete diff boundary, and C3's three.txt outside C2's. Sequential writers prevent simultaneous edits but do not preserve the claimed complete-diff isolation for parked changes. The owner-approved orchestration policy can motivate revising that design; it does not make the contradictory standing rule accurate. Align the standing isolation rule, its rationale and lifecycle instructions with the approved parked-change policy and its full-diff consequences before delivery. K6 also requires the lifecycle skills otherwise unchanged, so any necessary amendment to that constraint must go through the owner's material-revision gate rather than being inferred by an implementer.

The finish check at line 48 asks only whether a worker is currently writing; dispatch reconciliation is explicit only on resume at line 46. The original rehearsal ledger said all workers had returned and none was writing, but the subsequent session inventory still showed implement_c3 as pending_init. The addendum could not certify that every retained dispatch was incapable of writing; the parent then interrupted that pending dispatch after the run. That intervention must not be counted as cleanup performed by the orchestrator. No later product write or simultaneous writer is evidenced, so this does not falsify D9's bounded scheduling outcome or the literal no-current-writer condition. It does expose a concrete cleanup weakness: reconcile retained pending dispatches, as well as running workers, before claiming a run is finished, and record any unresolved dispatch explicitly.
